    The fitted year effects of ignitions and escapes, for hindcasts

    fittedYearEffects.Rd

    A hindcast of a fit year may use that year's fitted effect instead of a draw of yearSD (fireSense_burn's yearEffects = "fitted"); forecasts and NRV keep the draw. For each fit year y this gives the multiplier of the expected ignitions, u_I, and of the expected escapes of an ignited pixel, u_E, such that the hindcast's own draw (fireSense_burn: Poisson ignitions of mean u_I * lambda, each escaping with fireSenseUtils::escapeProbPerIgnition(u_E * e, u_I * lambda), counted in the core) expects the year's target counts. lambda and e are the fold-mean in-sample predictions (fireSenseUtils::foldMeanPrediction(), as fireSense_ignitionPredict predicts) of every pixel of the year, so the multipliers absorb at the year level both the models' in-sample bias and where the ignitions land (on pixels with a lower or higher escape mean than the observed ignitions).

    fittedYearEffects(ignitions, escapes)

    Arguments

    ignitions

    data.table of the ignition fit data, one row per pixel and year: pixelID, year, observed (ignitions), mean (the predicted ignitions of the whole pixel) and weight (its share in the core, exposureOf()).

    escapes

    data.table of the escape fit data: pixelID, year, observed (escapes) and mean (the predicted escapes if ignited), for the same pixels and years.

    Value

    A list of two data.frames, ignition and escape, one row per year: year, observed and expected (the core totals with no effect), priorSD (s), multiplier (the posterior mean, solved through the cap for escapes) and shape (of the posterior, a + observed; NA: no uncertainty).

    Details

    The target is not the observed count itself: a year with few expected events says little about its effect. With O_y ~ Poisson(u_y * mu_y) and a mean-one gamma prior on u_y of shape and rate a = 1 / (exp(s^2) - 1) (the variance of fireSenseUtils::yearEffectMultiplier(s, z)), the posterior mean is (a + O_y) / (a + mu_y), and the target is mu_y times it. s is fireSenseUtils::yearEffectSD(O, mu) of the same in-sample totals (empirical Bayes): the spread of the observed totals around these predictions, not the fit's yearSD, which is out of year and larger. A year with nothing expected keeps 1; s 0 (no more spread than Poisson) gives 1 everywhere. Escapes are solved after ignitions, with u_I applied, and cannot exceed the ignitions (the cap in escapeProbPerIgnition()): a target above that gives the multiplier at which every ignition escapes.

    The posterior is kept, not only its mean, so a hindcast's reps carry the uncertainty of the year's effect: shape = a + O_y is stored, and fireSense_burn multiplies each rep-year by multiplier * w, with w ~ Gamma(shape, rate = shape) (mean 1; one uniform per rep-year and process, qgamma(p, shape, shape)). For ignitions multiplier * w is then exactly a draw of the posterior Gamma(a + O_y, a + mu_y). For escapes w is the relative draw of the target count's posterior and is applied to the solved multiplier: exact at the mean and wherever the cap does not bind (it binds on about 1% of the expected escapes, ELF 6.6.2). shape is NA where the multiplier is fixed at 1 (nothing expected, or s 0): no draw.
